import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109908

$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.

*References:*
- [A109908](https://oeis.org/A109908)
-/

namespace OeisA109908

/--
$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 (n / 2))
  |>.image (fun k => k * (n - k) - 1)
  |>.filter Nat.Prime
  |>.sup id

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n > 3, a n > 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA109908

reformulations.difference: Lean implements the greatest prime of the stated form using natural-number arithmetic on the finite half-range 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, followed by Finset.sup id.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A positive prime value k(n−k)−1 with integer k and natural n forces 1 ≤ k < n. Reflecting k to n−k preserves the value and places a representative in the half-range. On this interval both natural-number subtractions agree with integer subtraction. Thus the filtered finset contains exactly the source's prime values; its supremum is their maximum, or 0 when empty. OEIS's Maple and PARI programs also use this half-range. The exact candidate-set equivalence, half/full-range image equality, and characterization of the resulting maximum were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry.

sources_consulted: Local Mathlib: Mathlib/Data/Finset/Lattice/Fold.lean, definitions and properties of Finset.sup.
review.notes: Checked all seven declarations. The complete OEIS entry states exactly “Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 3” and records verification through 10^9, consistent with research open. All five test theorems match the source's offset-1 table; the harmless extension a(0)=0 was also checked. Lean computations matched all 1,000 tested table entries. The final scratch file compiled successfully, including a sorry-free equivalence for the full conjecture. OEIS's HTML entry was blocked, so its complete text was read through the OEIS data mirror. A collateral Niu–Zhang preprint linked from A109909 was inaccessible through ResearchGate; only its DataCite metadata was read, and no status change was inferred from it.
